common_name: Chadwick Cherry Tomato (Vigorous Heirloom Red Cherry)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; Chadwick Cherry is an extremely vigorous, sprawling indeterminate vine that needs sturdy, tall staking and ample space.

directions: Transplant into well-drained, fertile soil in full sun after the last frost, providing tall, sturdy support for the exceptionally vigorous vines. Chadwick Cherry is a heirloom cherry tomato associated with biodynamic gardening pioneer Alan Chadwick, grown for its large, sprawling vines and heavy production of medium-sized, deep red, richly flavored cherry fruit with classic old-fashioned tomato taste. The plants are notably larger and more vigorous than many cherry tomato varieties, often reaching well over 8 feet if left unpruned, so give them generous space and a tall cage or trellis system. Harvest regularly once fruit turns fully red for the best flavor, and prune selectively to improve air circulation, since the dense vine growth can encourage fungal disease in humid climates.

common_name: Isis Candy Tomato (Bicolor Gold-and-Red Cherry Heirloom)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; Isis Candy is a productive indeterminate vine that benefits from staking or caging and bears heavily over a long season.

directions: Transplant into well-drained, fertile soil in full sun after the last frost, staking or caging the vigorous indeterminate vines for support. Isis Candy is a beloved heirloom cherry tomato producing round, golden-yellow fruit marbled and streaked with red, with a rich, sweet, well-balanced flavor that consistently ranks among the best-tasting cherry tomatoes in home garden trials. Plants are heavy, reliable producers over a long season, and the striking bicolor fruit makes an attractive addition to a mixed cherry tomato harvest or salad. Pick fruit as it fully colors for the best flavor, and water consistently to reduce splitting, since the thin skin is prone to cracking after heavy rain.
